items.title: Louis Tio Interview, 1960-10-26
items.q: My brother was the last that I had dealing with.

ctx.x: I know some people have told me that your brother seemed to have a French accent. I mean, certain people have told me how he would talk. They would start quoting, you know, saying certain things. And they would try to imitate a French accent. Do you remember? Did he have sort of a French?

Yes, he did, because I'll tell you why, because, you see, he was taught in French, in better words, he spoke French and English language. He spoke the French language frequently and he's read it. Also written it. He knew that because he learned that. Like I told you, I was kind of a little bad boy. I didn't, if they tried to catch me to do that, I was gone. Yeah, I didn't want to get part of that. I didn't, all I wanted to do, I love horses and I used to like to be around horses and I like to be doing something.…

Well, I was going to ask this about your uncle. People have told me that he sometimes didn't really like jazz so much that he liked classical music more. I know one man who was a pupil of Manuel Perez, Natty Dominique, who's in Chicago now. He knew your brother very well, too. And he told me when he was a kid, his father liked opera and his brother still lives over here on Robertson or some street down near there. And he used to be a good singer. And he said sometime your father would hear, your uncle would hear…
